cookieConsentText: Digitaltableteur uses cookies to improve your experience. Choosing "Accept all" enables optional analytics cookies. Selecting "Only essential" stores only the cookies required for the site to function.
cookiePolicyP1: We use cookies to remember your preferences and to analyze how our site is used. Essential cookies are saved automatically because the site cannot operate without them.
cookiePolicyP2: Analytics cookies are enabled only if you click "Accept all" on the modal. Choosing "Only essential" keeps these disabled. You can change your preference at any time through your browser settings.
cookiePolicyP3: For details about how we handle personal data and your rights under GDPR, please contact us.
cookiePolicyP4: To comply with EU law, we clearly separate cookies by purpose, keep a log of the choices made, and refresh consent at least every 13 months.
cookiePolicyCategoryEssential: Essential – required for login-free navigation, consent storage, and website security. These are first-party cookies with short lifetimes.
cookiePolicyCategoryAnalytics: Analytics – collect aggregated usage data via privacy-friendly tooling. They are stored only when you opt in.
cookiePolicyCategoryFunctional: Functional – remember language, theme, or embed settings to keep the experience consistent.
cookiePolicyCategoryMarketing: Marketing/community – enable previews from services like Substack or Instagram. Disabled unless you consent.
cookiePolicyConsentBody: Use the banner to revise your choice. You can also reopen it by clearing the "cookieConsent" entry in your browser’s storage or contacting mail@digitaltableteur.com so we can reset your preference.
cookiePolicyAiReference: Parts of the site are created or tested with AI-assisted tooling. Details about those workflows are listed in our
aiPolicyMetaDescription: Read how Digitaltableteur uses AI-assisted tools, the safeguards we apply, and your rights under EU law.
aiPolicyIntro: We apply AI-assisted services carefully and in line with the EU AI Act and GDPR. Humans stay responsible for every deliverable, and we track each tool that touches client or visitor data.
aiPolicyUseCaseDesign: Design exploration – generating alternative layouts or colour palettes for internal review. AI suggestions are always reviewed by a senior designer before implementation.
aiPolicyUseCaseContent: Editorial assistance – drafting article outlines, alt texts, or translations that are later fact-checked and edited by a human.
aiPolicyUseCaseOperations: Quality assurance – analysing anonymised support tickets and telemetry to improve accessibility and performance.
aiPolicyDataTitle: Data we send to AI providers
aiPolicyDataBody: We only share the prompts necessary for the task at hand, remove personal identifiers whenever possible, and opt out of provider-side training. Sensitive production data is never sent to public models.
aiPolicySafeguardHumanReview: Human review – every AI output is validated by an accountable team member before being published or delivered to a client.
aiPolicySafeguardDataMinimisation: Data minimisation – prompts are truncated, masked, or sampled so that individuals cannot be identified.
aiPolicySafeguardVendorReview: Vendor review – we only use providers that offer EU-grade security and data processing agreements.
aiPolicyRightInformation: Right to information – you can ask us which AI systems touched your project or data at any time.
aiPolicyRightObjection: Right to object – you may request that we avoid AI-assisted tooling in your assignment. We will confirm feasibility and document the alternative workflow.
aiPolicyRightErasure: Right to erasure – if AI tooling touched personal data, you can request deletion or expect it to follow the retention limits in our contract.
aiPolicyRightsFooter: To exercise these rights, email mail@digitaltableteur.com or contact us via the channels listed in the privacy policy.

docsThemeSubtitle: How global styles, CSS variables, and translations work together across the app.
docsThemePipelineStep1: Design tokens are defined as CSS custom properties in src/styles/variables.css.
docsThemePipelineStep2: ThemeProvider reads and updates the active theme via context and body class toggles.
docsThemePipelineStep3: Storybook decorators wrap stories with ThemeProvider so toolbar toggles reflect instantly.
docsThemePipelineTipVariables: Use getComputedStyle to read live token values when rendering charts or visualizations.
docsThemePipelineTipTokens: Prefer CSS variables over hard-coded colours so both themes stay in sync.
docsThemePipelineTipForcedTheme: When embedding components externally, honour the forcedTheme prop to avoid mismatches.
docsLocalePipelineStep1: i18next dynamically imports translation bundles from src/locales/{lang}/translation.json.
docsLocalePipelineStep2: Language switches persist via cookies/localStorage and are restored on load.
docsLocalePipelineStep3: Storybook’s globe toolbar switches the active language for every story.
docsLocaleTipUseTranslation: Use the useTranslation hook inside components and stories.
docsLocaleTipParity: Always update English, Finnish, and Swedish translations together to satisfy coverage tests.
docsLocaleTipStoryCopy: For Storybook-only copy, reuse existing keys where sensible to keep phrasing consistent.
docsTestingCommandTest: npm run test – run Vitest across units and integrations.
docsTestingCommandA11y: npm run test:a11y – run page and Storybook accessibility audits.
docsTestingCommandStorybook: npm run storybook – manually verify theme/locale behaviour when needed.
